clues.clue: The borough takes its 'the' and its name from this Swedish settler who farmed here in 1639.
clues.reveal: Jonas Bronck. The Swedish settler whose 1639 farm gave 'Bronck's River,' and later The Bronx, its name.

clues.clue: The Bronx is the only NYC borough located on this larger landmass rather than an island.
clues.reveal: The Mainland. The Bronx is the only borough on the U.S. mainland; all the others sit on islands.

clues.clue: Before 1898 the Bronx belonged to this neighboring county to the north.
clues.reveal: Westchester. The Bronx was part of Westchester County until the area was annexed to New York City in the late 1800s.

clues.clue: A 1973 party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in CB5 is credited as the birthplace of this music genre.
clues.reveal: Hip Hop (CB5, Morris Heights). DJ Kool Herc's August 1973 party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is widely called the birthplace of hip hop.

clues.clue: CB4's Art Deco boulevard, modeled on the Champs-Elysees, is known as the Bronx's grand one.
clues.reveal: Grand Concourse (CB4). Built in the early 1900s and modeled on the Champs-Elysees; it holds one of America's great Art Deco collections.

clues.clue: This poet wrote 'Annabel Lee' at his cottage on the Grand Concourse in what is now CB6.
clues.reveal: Edgar Allan Poe. He spent his last years in a Bronx cottage, now Poe Cottage, where he wrote 'Annabel Lee.'

clues.clue: Opened in 1923 in CB4 and called 'The House That Ruth Built,' it is home to a 27-time champion team.
clues.reveal: Yankee Stadium (CB4). Opened in 1923, nicknamed 'The House That Ruth Built'; home of the New York Yankees.

clues.clue: CB6 is home to this 250-acre zoo, one of the largest metropolitan zoos in the United States.
clues.reveal: Bronx Zoo (CB6). Opened in 1899, it is among the largest metropolitan zoos in the country.

clues.clue: Next to the zoo in CB6, this 250-acre garden is a National Historic Landmark founded in 1891.
clues.reveal: New York Botanical Garden (CB6). Founded in 1891, a National Historic Landmark beside the Bronx Zoo.

clues.clue: CB6's Arthur Avenue is widely called the borough's real version of this Manhattan ethnic enclave.
clues.reveal: Little Italy (CB6, Arthur Avenue). Belmont's Arthur Avenue is often called the Bronx's, and the city's, real Little Italy.

clues.clue: CB8's Riverdale is the leafy, hilly northwest corner once home to JFK and writer Mark Twain.
clues.reveal: Riverdale (CB8). The wooded, hilly northwest Bronx neighborhood, historically home to notable residents including a young John F. Kennedy.

clues.clue: CB10's nautical enclave, reached by a single bridge, feels more like a New England fishing village.
clues.reveal: City Island (CB10). A small maritime community in the western Long Island Sound, known for seafood and boatbuilding.
